title: Choice of geometry with identity direct-image section comparisons
statement: For every prime l, finite extension E of Q_l, schemes X,Y and f:X to Y, there exist Base b and Geometry g [def-sp-tower-shriek-data] such that generic.levelPushUnderlying acts identically on every underlying module section at every finite level. This does not construct any coefficient-unit map or assert any equation between such maps.

source.place: clause (2), finite unit and tensor maps and their transposes

proof.text: Choose the Base from strictBaseCoordinates, retaining its calculus at both schemes. Use finite_sectionInverseImages to obtain the compatible prescribed finite pullbacks and canonical adjunctions. Define the level push-underlying isomorphism by identity components; its action on every section is reflexivity.

Use finite-limit preservation of the set inverse image. Apply ordinaryInverseSystem_exists and ordinaryDirectSystem_exists to the supplied finite data. Their component Hom bijections are natural by levelwise naturality and faithful ordinary evaluation. Build the system adjunction from these bijections and derive its level unit formula from homEquiv_component. Assemble GeometryOrdinary, retaining all prescribed finite fields.

Apply semilinearGeometryEvaluation and semilinearGeometryTensor to this fixed ordinary realization and the two Base calculi. Assemble Geometry using the canonical derived adjunctions and their representative transpose formula. Derive the pull-transition formula, then its direct-image mate and the projection evaluation identity. Transport finite pull evaluation across the equality of its module functor with the canonical pullback; equality elimination proves that this preserves the generic comparison. Bundle the resulting Geometry in SpTowerShriek.Geometry. Its level push-underlying isomorphism is still identity, proving the claimed HEq by reflexivity.

Supply ordinaryUnitTransition for the explicit Geometry constructor. The inverse-system transition equation conjugates the pulled transition to the inverse image of the original transition followed by its restriction comparison. The restriction-underlying identity cancels the inverse-image underlying isomorphisms. The finite transpose normalization then reduces compatibility to naturality of the original set-sheaf adjunction. Apply it to every section, retaining the HEq carrier premise, and transport the complete finite adjunction packages to the actual constant-ring coordinates. No root, Chern datum or line comparison is involved.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_sectionGeometry {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    ∃ b : SpTowerShriek.Base l E, ∃ g : SpTowerShriek.Geometry l E b f,
      ∀ (n : ℕ)
        (N : SemilinearSections.Mod.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
          (g.generic.coefficients n)) (U : Y.ProEtᵒᵖ)
        (x : ((SemilinearSections.underlying.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
          (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (SpTowerShriek.B l E Y n)).obj
            ((g.generic.levelPush n).obj N)).obj.obj U),
        HEq (((g.generic.levelPushUnderlying n).hom.app N).hom.app U x) x
